session.question: How does the theme of "Green Cluod Computing" connect the discussion of Green IoT with the systematic survey of energy-efficient techniques in sustainabl cloud computing, especially regarding why data centers and cloud technologies are being optimized for lower energy use and reduced environmental harm?
session.answer:
Green IoT and Green Cloud Computing are linked by a shared objective: reducing the energy footprint of computation, communication, and storage while maintaining acceptable service quality. In Green IoT, resource-constrained devices rely on edge, fog, and cloud support to offload processing, aggregate data, and manage workloads efficiently; this makes cloud-side optimization a necessary part of end-to-end sustainability. The same energy-aware techniques discussed for massive IoT networks—task offloading, virtualization, scheduling, energy harvesting, and cooling optimization—extend naturally into cloud infrastructures. (alsharif2024acomprehensivesurvey chunk 1)

The systematic survey shows why cloud/data-center optimization is central to this agenda. Data centers consume large amounts of electricity, much of which is converted into heat, increasing cooling demand, reliability issues, and carbon emissions. The survey therefore emphasizes software-level techniques such as VM virtualization and consolidation, power-aware control, bio-inspired methods, and thermal management to reduce energy use and CO2 footprints with minimal infrastructure overhead. (bharany2022asystematicsurvey chunk 1)

Green data center practices further explain the motivation: energy-efficient hardware, renewable energy integration, advanced cooling, and optimized resource allocation lower operational cost and environmental harm, while AI-enabled management improves cooling and workload prediction. Together, these sources show that Green Cloud Computing is the infrastructural enabler of Green IoT, because efficient clouds are required to process IoT data sustainably and to reduce fossil-fuel-driven emissions across the computing stack. (chidolue2024greendatacenters chunk 1, buyya2023energy‐efficiencyandsustainability chunk 1)

session.context:
pqac-eaf376f6: The excerpt describes a systematic survey on energy-efficient techniques in sustainable cloud computing, motivated by the environmental impact of high energy consumption and CO2 emissions from data centers, computing devices, and network equipment. It explains that these systems rely heavily on fossil-fuel-based power generation, contributing to global warming, ozone depletion, and other harms. The paper reviews 119 primary studies and categorizes green cloud techniques such as VM virtualization and consolidation, power-aware methods, bio-inspired methods, and thermal management. It emphasizes software-level approaches because they require less infrastructure and are less prone to failure, helping reduce energy use and CO2 footprints in cloud data centers.
From Salil Bharany, Sandeep Sharma, Osamah Ibrahim Khalaf, Ghaida Muttashar Abdulsahib, Abeer S. Al Humaimeedy, Theyazn H. H. Aldhyani, Mashael Maashi, and Hasan Alkahtani. A systematic survey on energy-efficient techniques in sustainable cloud computing. Sustainability, 2022. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/su14106256, doi:10.3390/su14106256.

pqac-aa753a0b: The excerpt describes green data centers as a sustainability-focused approach to energy-efficient IT infrastructure. It highlights key practices: using energy-efficient hardware and virtualization, integrating renewable energy to reduce fossil-fuel dependence, employing advanced cooling methods like liquid immersion, hot aisle containment, and free air cooling, and optimizing resources so energy is used judiciously. It also notes benefits such as reduced operational costs, better brand image, and compliance with environmental regulations, while mentioning challenges like upfront costs and renewable-grid integration. Emerging trends include AI and edge computing for cooling optimization, peak workload prediction, and dynamic resource management. This is directly relevant to how cloud/data center technologies are optimized to lower energy use and environmental harm.
From Onyinyechukwu Chidolue, Peter Efosa Ohenhen, Aniekan Akpan Umoh, Bright Ngozichukwu, Adetomilola Victoria Fafure, and Kenneth Ifeanyi Ibekwe. Green data centers: sustainable practices for energy-efficient it infrastructure. Engineering Science & Technology Journal, 2024. URL: https://doi.org/10.51594/estj.v5i1.730, doi:10.51594/estj.v5i1.730.

pqac-d7c205e4: The excerpt explains that energy efficiency and green computing are central to building sustainable massive IoT networks. It says IoT devices often have limited computational power and energy, so computing technologies like edge, fog, and cloud are used to conserve energy while supporting data collection and processing. The survey covers energy-saving techniques in computing environments, including energy-aware architecture, data aggregation and compression, low-power hardware, energy-aware scheduling, task offloading, turning unused resources on/off, virtualization, energy harvesting, and cooling optimization. It frames these as part of a roadmap for sustainable computing, which aligns with Green Cloud Computing and reduced environmental impact.
From Mohammed H. Alsharif, Anabi Hilary Kelechi, Abu Jahid, Raju Kannadasan, Manish Kumar Singla, Jyoti Gupta, and Zong Woo Geem. A comprehensive survey of energy-efficient computing to enable sustainable massive iot networks. Alexandria Engineering Journal, 2024. URL: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.aej.2024.01.067, doi:10.1016/j.aej.2024.01.067.

pqac-d0625853: The excerpt explains that energy-efficient computing, or green computing, is essential for sustainable massive IoT networks because IoT devices have limited power and need support for data collection, processing, and storage. It highlights green computing across edge, fog, and cloud environments and lists techniques such as energy-aware architecture, task offloading, virtualization, energy harvesting, and cooling optimization. Although it does not explicitly define Green IoT vs. Green Cloud Computing, it suggests they are related through the shared goal of improving energy efficiency and sustainability. Green cloud computing is implied to support IoT by providing efficient data-center-based computing and storage, helping reduce overall energy use and environmental impact.
From Mohammed H. Alsharif, Anabi Hilary Kelechi, Abu Jahid, Raju Kannadasan, Manish Kumar Singla, Jyoti Gupta, and Zong Woo Geem. A comprehensive survey of energy-efficient computing to enable sustainable massive iot networks. Alexandria Engineering Journal, 2024. URL: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.aej.2024.01.067, doi:10.1016/j.aej.2024.01.067.

pqac-c16bad62: The excerpt explains that cloud computing has become essential infrastructure but has also created a major global energy challenge. Data centres supporting cloud services now consume enormous amounts of electricity, with projections of up to 20% of global electricity use and 5.5% of carbon emissions by 2025. Much of this energy becomes heat, causing reliability problems, shorter device lifespans, and higher cooling demand. The paper argues that future cloud systems must be energy-efficient and environmentally sustainable while still maintaining service quality. It proposes a learning-centric approach and integrated resource/workload management to reduce energy consumption and carbon footprint, aligning with green cloud computing goals.
From Rajkumar Buyya, Shashikant Ilager, and Patricia Arroba. Energy‐efficiency and sustainability in new generation cloud computing: a vision and directions for integrated management of data centre resources and workloads. Software Practice and Experience, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.1002/spe.3248, doi:10.1002/spe.3248.

contexts.context: The excerpt describes research on environmentally sustainable federated cloud computing, emphasizing that data centers consume significant energy and contribute to global carbon emissions. It states that reducing energy consumption and carbon emissions in data centers is crucial for sustainable development, and that traditional cloud computing has reached a bottleneck because of high energy use. The paper proposes ERLFC, a reinforcement-learning-based task scheduling framework for federated clouds that leverages geographic differences among data centers to optimize assignment decisions. Factors include energy consumption, cooling method, waiting time, energy type, emission ratio, and total current energy use. Simulation results show ERLFC reduces energy consumption and emissions compared with several baselines.

session.formatted_answer:
Question: How does the theme of "Green Cluod Computing" connect the discussion of Green IoT with the systematic survey of energy-efficient techniques in sustainabl cloud computing, especially regarding why data centers and cloud technologies are being optimized for lower energy use and reduced environmental harm?

Green IoT and Green Cloud Computing are linked by a shared objective: reducing the energy footprint of computation, communication, and storage while maintaining acceptable service quality. In Green IoT, resource-constrained devices rely on edge, fog, and cloud support to offload processing, aggregate data, and manage workloads efficiently; this makes cloud-side optimization a necessary part of end-to-end sustainability. The same energy-aware techniques discussed for massive IoT networks—task offloading, virtualization, scheduling, energy harvesting, and cooling optimization—extend naturally into cloud infrastructures. (alsharif2024acomprehensivesurvey chunk 1)

The systematic survey shows why cloud/data-center optimization is central to this agenda. Data centers consume large amounts of electricity, much of which is converted into heat, increasing cooling demand, reliability issues, and carbon emissions. The survey therefore emphasizes software-level techniques such as VM virtualization and consolidation, power-aware control, bio-inspired methods, and thermal management to reduce energy use and CO2 footprints with minimal infrastructure overhead. (bharany2022asystematicsurvey chunk 1)

Green data center practices further explain the motivation: energy-efficient hardware, renewable energy integration, advanced cooling, and optimized resource allocation lower operational cost and environmental harm, while AI-enabled management improves cooling and workload prediction. Together, these sources show that Green Cloud Computing is the infrastructural enabler of Green IoT, because efficient clouds are required to process IoT data sustainably and to reduce fossil-fuel-driven emissions across the computing stack. (chidolue2024greendatacenters chunk 1, buyya2023energy‐efficiencyandsustainability chunk 1)
